findings.description: The inline policy grants full service-wide access (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) against Resource "*", with no conditions or resource scoping. This permits account-wide data exfiltration and destruction (e.g. s3:PutBucketPolicy to make any bucket public, s3:GetObject/DeleteObject on all buckets) and lateral movement via lambda:UpdateFunctionCode on existing functions or launching EC2 instances, violating least privilege.

Terraform creates a permanent IAM access key for a highly privileged user. With no pgp_key supplied, the plaintext secret access key is persisted in Terraform state, exposing an unrotated, near-administrative credential to everyone with state file access.

The output "svc_deploy_key_material" exports access key material without sensitive = true, so the value is rendered in plan/apply console output and captured in CI/CD logs and artifacts where it is readable by anyone with pipeline access.

The IAM user backing these broad permissions has no permissions boundary, no MFA requirement, and relies on static keys rather than a federated or assumable role, leaving a standing high-privilege identity with no compensating access controls.
